# Submission note — an untouched knob crosses 60% vs Google (score 1,199,970,432)

## 1. Initial context and goal

Entering this submission the promoted frontier was **1,200,072,672** at `3f57ea5`
(Q = 1278, T = 939,024, baked nonce `79297`). That commit differs from my own `2f4a7d7`
(Q = 1278, T = 939,026) in the nonce constant *and nothing else* — a whitespace-insensitive
diff of the two is one line — so it is a pure nonce-lottery step worth 2,556 score.

The goal was specific: cross **60% reduction against Google's published low-gate Pareto
point of 3.0 × 10⁹**. That threshold is score `< 1,200,000,000` exactly, and the frontier sat
at 1,200,072,672 — i.e. **59.9976%**, missing by 72,672 (0.006%). At Q = 1278 that is a
budget of only **57 executed Toffoli**.

Result: **1,199,970,432** (`toffoli 938944 × qubits 1278`), i.e. **−102,240 (−0.0085%)**
against `3f57ea5`, and **60.0010%** against 3.0 × 10⁹ — the threshold is crossed with
29,568 of margin.

## 2. Where the 57 Toffoli came from

A nonce lottery has a spread of roughly ±6 executed Toffoli at this depth — an order of
magnitude too small. The depth ladder (`SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL`) was already spent: the next
half-round is worth ~375 Toffoli but its λ is 16.12, needing ~10 M candidate nonces.

So instead of pushing either known axis I enumerated the whole tunable surface and swept it
with a static estimator. `grep` over the shipped source gives the complete knob list:

    SUB4_PP_PEAK 1278            SUB4_PP_REPLAY_CHUNK 96
    SUB4_PP_R1 298               SUB4_PP_REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE 23
    SUB4_PP_R2 613               SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE 24
    SUB4_PP_ROUNDS 700           SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW 54
    SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL           SUB4_PP_ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW 28
    SUB4_APPLY_STRIP / SUB4_NO_GAP (presence flags)

`SUB4_PP_ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW` had never been moved. It turns out to be an almost perfectly
linear dial: each step of 1 is worth exactly **8 executed Toffoli = 10,224 score**.

## 3. The trap the sweep produced, and why λ has to gate everything

The static sweep's headline result was not this knob. It was
`SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW = 50`, showing **−7,115,904 (−0.59%)** — a single env change
apparently worth ten times the whole day's grind. It is worthless:

| knob setting | Toffoli gain | λ_total | P(clean) | candidates needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW=50 | −7,115,904 | **39.45** | 7 × 10⁻¹⁸ | impossible |
| REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW=52 | −3,557,952 | 19.91 | 2.2 × 10⁻⁹ | ~450 M |
| REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE=20 | −4,607,190 | 17.80 | 1.9 × 10⁻⁸ | ~54 M |
| REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE=21 | −2,664,630 | 14.52 | 4.9 × 10⁻⁷ | ~2.0 M |
| **ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW=20** | **−81,792** | **10.99** | 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ | **~59 K** |

Every one of these knobs is a truncation dial: shrinking it removes carry-chain work and
adds convergence failures. A static op-count scan measures the gain and is *completely blind*
to the cost, and the shipped defaults sit where they do precisely because λ explodes below
them. The monotone giveaway is visible in the numbers — fold 50 < 52 < 53 < 54(shipped) —
and the correct reading of a large static gain is "suspect a λ cliff", not "free win".

Concretely: the option with 87× more Toffoli gain than the one submitted is
**10¹³ times less likely** to yield a submittable nonce.

## 8. Failures and course corrections

**Two real bugs, both caught by md5 discipline rather than by reading diffs.**

*A confirmation script that verified the wrong circuit.* `confirm.sh` derived its env
override as `SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL=${T#m}` — fine for tiers named `m694`, but for tier `ep20`
it set `SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL=ep20` (unparseable, silently falling back to the default) and
never set the endpoint window at all. It therefore rebuilt the *shipped* circuit with the new
nonce, which duly failed 13/8. For about a minute this looked like a false positive from the
prefilter. It was not: with the correct override the same nonce is 0/0/0. The script now
enumerates every tier naming explicitly and aborts on an unrecognised one rather than
guessing.

*A `sed` that silently did nothing.* My first attempt to stage this submission was made
while the head moved from `f836a70` to `3f57ea5`. The nonce substitution pattern targeted the
old constant, did not match, and left the file unchanged — so the build produced the previous
circuit while the source diff *looked* right (only the endpoint line appeared). The md5
mismatch against the confirmed build caught it. In my previous note I had written that for a
constant-only change "only byte equality of the emitted stream distinguishes applied from
appeared-to-apply"; this is that failure mode arriving in practice. Both constant edits are
now asserted to have changed their file before the build runs.

**λ estimate was optimistic.** ep20's λ came from 4 draws (10.99). The hunt then screened
185,473 nonces before hitting, where λ = 10.99 predicts ~59,000 (P(no hit by then) = 4.3%).
The implied λ is nearer 12.5. Four draws is too few; the ±1.7 standard error I noted was
real and I should have used it to widen the estimate rather than quoting the point value.

**Previously reported and still standing:** my earlier claim that packing the `Op` record
would give ~3.5× was wrong — measured 1.19× — and all three mechanistic explanations
(memory bandwidth, hyperthreading, NUMA) were disproved by direct measurement. The scaling
curve is a smooth contention slope: 1.14 s/nonce at 1 worker, 1.96 s at 118.

## 9. Caveats

- ep20's threshold margin (29,568 as drawn) depends on the nonce. The *tier* only clears by
  6,564, so this specific result should not be read as "ep20 crosses 60%" — ep18 is the
  setting that does so robustly.
- λ figures rest on 4 draws per setting and are indicative only.
- This spends λ budget: it makes the next rung harder for whoever grinds after it.
- `pp-hunt` is a prefilter and is never authoritative; every number here comes from
  `eval_circuit`, twice, on two hosts.
- The three big static gains in §3 are not disproved as *ideas* — they are disproved as
  *reachable* at their measured λ. A change that lowers λ makes them live again.

## 10. Learning

The tunable surface was substantially unexplored: one knob nobody had moved was worth exactly
the 57 Toffoli needed to cross a round-number threshold, and it was found by enumeration plus
a free static estimator, not by deeper truncation of the axis everyone was already pushing.
Enumerate the whole knob list before assuming the frontier direction is the only direction.

The corollary is the discipline in §3: on this benchmark a static gate count is a *lower
bound on cost*, never a score. Any sweep over truncation knobs must be paired with a λ
measurement before a single core is committed, because the ranking by gain and the ranking by
expected value are close to inverted.

## 11. Next steps

1. `SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE = 21` is the next real target: **−2,664,630 (−0.22%)** at
   λ = 14.52, about 2 M candidates ≈ 9 hours on this host. That is an overnight job and by far
   the largest reachable item found today.
2. `SUB4_PP_REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE = 20` (−4,607,190) needs ~54 M candidates — a fleet, not a
   single host.
3. Combine axes: the endpoint window is orthogonal to the depth ladder and to `R1`/`PEAK`, so
   a joint sweep (ep, R1, PEAK) is likely to beat coordinate-wise tuning. `R1` was swept at
   PEAK = 1278 and 298 is already optimal there, but the landscape is jagged (297 is worse
   than both 296 and 298), so a joint sweep is not a formality.
4. Reducing λ itself remains the highest-leverage direction: every −1.0 multiplies hunt yield
   by *e*, and it is what would make §3's large gains reachable.
